author: Mr_Wiggles
quote:
The best final fantasy game released within the last 25 years (since FFX maybe?). It remains mostly faithful to the original content while expanding upon it in new and interesting ways. 

More to the point, this is probably the most perfectly designed open-world game I have ever played. It introduces massive modular areas that employ every tact of game design from challenge battles, item collection, quest progression, discoveries and more to make exploration actually feel rewarding. Areas that are at first feel overwhelming are soon completed, but the game does a good job of not letting you overstep by limiting you within certain regions.

It also has a ridiculous number of mini-games, Queens Blood (a pretty decent card game), battle arenas and VR simulations. Some people complain about the number and difficulty, however in my opinion it only serves to add a massive amount of content and character to the world. Plus if you really don't like them most mini-games are optional beyond the most basic completion.

On a casual playthrough you can get away with just about any build... then... there is hard-mode (and it is HARD), which on a second playthrough is the first time I actually grasped the amazing depth of the combat and Materia systems. There are challenge battles that seem impossibly difficult, and even with good strategy you need great execution to pull it off, but the reward is that much greater when you finally do it.

The one thing that might turn people off is that the plot becomes ridiculously convoluted, and you'll find yourself turning to wikis to try and figure it out. Additionally, that pivotal scene (yes, if you played the original you know what I'm talking about) honestly hits a lot weaker than it's 1997 counterpart. 

Overall it takes the best of part I, improves and massively expands it, to fantastic results. Hopefully they don't stray too much from this formula in part III.

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote:
A massive downgrade in every possible category except graphics. The developers are a perfect case study for AI replacing human jobs because even middling generative slop would be an improvement.

The writers clearly have no direction and are petrified to the obvious lanes needed to progress a game like this. They somehow manage to sterilize human relations to embarrassing levels while degrading and objectifying others. They want you to cause chaos and destruction, oh.. but you can't shoot their master race of protected people (apparently its fine to murder everyone else in their opinion). The story is cluttered with garbage menial tasks. The game tries its hardest to push the mundane in your face and hide any fun far away from you... and just for good measure throw in mediocre performance and numerous glitches. 

I'm sure it will eventually be on PC modded to fix a lot of the garbage, but until then steer clear.

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote: The only positive is beautiful art and animation. Unfortunately the gameplay is basic and lackluster. However, worst of all is the bigoted story of victim-hood tropes, a tiresome narrative that's been told a million times with nothing new to offer. Perhaps nearly 100 years ago, when Disney started doing animation like this, it could have been semi-relevant. Nowadays, perhaps driven by lack of purpose, the devs just want to resurrect a dead specter of a movement to feed their narcissism.

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote: Really expected to like this, I have been searching for new titles akin to the classic Pokemon games...this is not it. For starters there a numerous technical issues, from excessive loading times to poor frame rates and graphical glitches. Why can the Nintendo DS from 20 years ago provide a smoother experience!?! Additionally, the art style is uninspired and lacks stylization. I also found some of the music choices baffling, the soundtrack for the first town was so bad I had to turn the volume off to avoid headache. Nevertheless, I still find some enjoyment in the concept and basic gameplay, however there are far better Pokemon clones available... skip this one.

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote: This DLC is exactly what bloodborne needed to make the experience complete. The added environments, gear and enemies perfectly complement the base game and complete the difficulty curve, which the original lacked at the end. Fear the old blood!

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote: Too much **** thing? Maybe. Elden Ring takes the souls formula and improves on it in some ways, but hinders it in others. The primary offender for me is making the into a vastly more open-world structure. The experience seems to lose some of the carefully curated design and structure of its predecessors. Nevertheless, the gameplay and creativity shines through, delivering one of the best experiences available for the current generation of consoles.

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote: Remake done right. Almost everything is better than the original. The graphics are far more detailed and the atmosphere is improved by the new lighting. The weapons are better balances and you now acquire them through exploration, the sections of the ship feel more connected, and the controls are significantly improved (especially the zero-g sections). Everything combined breathes new life into this classic.

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote: Why do the characters get slightly uglier with every new version? At least the environments have a lot more detail.. they probably would look a lot better but unfortunately they washed out the lighting. I guess Naughty Dog doesn't have any real play but to sell you the same junk over and over, since they clearly aren't interested in hiring competent writers to make their developers efforts worthwhile.
game_title: The Last of Us Part I

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote:
Remastering the last of us part II is like spray-painting a dung heap. It might look slightly better, but its still the same excrement underneath. 

However, the game isn't even remastered.. in fact its virtually the same game (with very minor upgrades) running at a higher resolution. It seems even the studio didn't care enough about the game to put any effort in.
game_title: The Last of Us Part II Remastered

author: Mr_Wiggles
quote: Candidate for the worst sequel of all time. Everything you loved about the first game is dead (literally) and the story dribbles onward nonsensically with the most unlikable characters imaginable. Yes, the graphics and gameplay are improved, but they were never great to begin with. All the mechanics are pretty generic at this point and hundreds of games do them better. The heart and soul of the original has been replace with a script and characters that were written by a 'bot' that doesn't understand what a human being is. The only good news is that Banjo-Kazooie: nuts and bolts now looks like a pretty good sequel in comparison.
game_title: The Last of Us Part II
